content:
Earlier in July this year, Apple updated its TestFlight app with basic search functionality. While you might think such a simple update would be widely welcomed, the same version of TestFlight introduced a rather annoying bug for many users.

Personally, I wasn't affected by this bug, at least not that I noticed. So at the time, I thought the TestFlight update, though simple, was a significant step forward.

Sometimes, small changes can have a big impact. This is especially true for users with a large number of pre-release software testing versions when it comes to Apple's latest TestFlight update. Apple has just updated TestFlight for iPhone, iPad, Mac, and other platforms. The new version 4.3 added a "search bar for quickly finding apps".

Looking back, I did notice some oddities, which I've noted at the end of the article (though my assessment turned out to be the opposite):

I think the reason I overlooked that this was actually a bug was because when I merged my iCloud and App Store Apple accounts last year, I was left with a batch of TestFlight testing records going back several years. The process was a hassle, but worth it for me.

In any case, the TestFlight bug did not escape the notice of John Vorhees at MacStories:

So when I read Zac Hall's article at 9to5Mac about TestFlight getting a search bar, you can imagine my excitement. I thought, "Finally!" I immediately dropped what I was doing and updated the app on the spot. [...] Unfortunately, there's a big "but" to this story. Previously, TestFlight's beta builds were listed in reverse chronological order, which I really liked. [...] Now, the expired beta builds have been mixed in with the ongoing beta builds list, sorted alphabetically, and the expired beta list seems to have expanded to cover every single beta version I've ever participated in. I did a rough count — for me it's close to 800 app entries. As you can imagine, very few of the entries in the list are for ongoing betas. The search function certainly helps, but you can no longer just scroll through the list.

Then in August, John Gruber wrote an article on Daring Fireball specifically about the TestFlight update and the bug:

Last night, more than a month after the bug appeared (and was spotted by Vorhees), Apple finally updated TestFlight for the first time. Although the update notes only mention bug fixes, the update does correct the relevant bug.

TestFlight version 4.3.1 is precisely the fix provided for users affected by this regression issue.
